data.title: Researchers find a way to make the HIV virus visible within white blood cells
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 研究人员在寻找HIV治愈方法方面取得了突破，发现了一种迫使病毒从隐藏的白细胞中显现的新方法，为彻底清除体内HIV铺平了道路。HIV能够藏匿于特定白细胞内，使得病毒在体内形成潜伏库，难以被免疫系统或药物清除。来自墨尔本彼得·多尔蒂感染与免疫研究所的团队利用mRNA技术，通过特制的脂肪泡将mRNA送入隐藏HIV的细胞，使其揭示病毒。这种新型的脂质纳米颗粒（LNP X）成功解决了此前无法将mRNA送入此类细胞的难题。尽管还需进一步研究以确定揭示病毒是否足以让免疫系统消灭它，但这一发现为HIV治愈带来了新希望。研究还在早期阶段，距离临床应用还需多年研究和试验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HIV治疗的新方法及其潜在应用和限制

不同观点：
• [w10-1] 认为该研究虽然展示了通过封装mRNA激活潜伏HIV细胞的方法，但以往类似尝试均未成功清除病毒库。该方法可能更多是验证一种技术的可行性，而非直接用于治愈HIV。还提到HIV治疗的高昂成本使其成为长期治疗，药物公司可能更关注资金支持。
  
• [blindriver] 认为制药公司缺乏治愈HIV的动力，因为治愈性治疗不如长期的月度治疗（如Ozempic）对 Wall Street 有吸引力。引用Gilead治愈丙型肝炎却遭到批评的例子，暗示经济利益影响HIV治愈的研发。

• [bawolff] 提出该方法是否可以应用于其他潜伏性病毒，如带状疱疹或疱疹病毒，表明该技术可能具有更广泛的应用前景。

• [kylehotchkiss] 提到该技术在HIV上的成功是否可以延伸至其他疾病，如结核病和麻风病，表明了对技术扩展应用的期待。

• [istjohn] 引用Tomáš Hanke教授的观点，质疑将RNA导入白细胞的难度，并认为希望通过这种方式触及所有潜伏HIV的细胞“ merely a dream”（仅仅是个梦想），暗示该方法的实际效果可能有限。

• [user____name] 提到另一个近期的突破，提供额外研究支持讨论，表明科学界在不断取得进展。

• [hackernoops] 简单表示该发展是积极的，没有深入讨论，但持乐观态度。

补充讨论：
- 经济利益与HIV治愈研究之间的关系是一个争议焦点，尤其是制药公司是否真正愿意投入资源寻找治愈方案，还是更倾向于维持长期治疗方案。
- 该技术是否能广泛应用于其他潜伏性病毒疾病也是讨论的一个扩展方向。
- 不同评论对该研究实际效果的预期存在分歧，部分评论持怀疑态度，而其他评论则较为乐观。

争议焦点：制药公司是否真正有动力去治愈HIV，以及该新方法的实际应用效果。

An illustration of HIV virus particles. The virus has the ability to conceal itself within certain white blood cells.
Illustration: Ruslanas Baranauskas/Science Photo Library/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
An illustration of HIV virus particles. The virus has the ability to conceal itself within certain white blood cells.
Illustration: Ruslanas Baranauskas/Science Photo Library/Getty Images
Global development
Breakthrough in search for HIV cure leaves researchers ‘overwhelmed’
Exclusive: Melbourne team demonstrates way to make the virus visible within white blood cells, paving the way to fully clear it from the body
Supported by
About this content
Kat Lay
Global health correspondent
Thu 5 Jun 2025 01.00 EDT
Last modified on Fri 6 Jun 2025 00.25 EDT
Share
A cure for HIV could be a step closer after researchers found a new way to force the virus out of hiding inside human cells.
The virus’s ability to conceal itself inside certain white blood cells has been one of the main challenges for scientists looking for a cure. It means there is a reservoir of the HIV in the body, capable of reactivation, that neither the immune system nor drugs can tackle.
Now researchers from the Peter Doherty Institute for Infection and Immunity in Melbourne, have demonstrated a way to make the virus visible, paving the way to fully clear it from the body.
It is based on mRNA technology, which came to prominence during the Covid-19 pandemic
when it was used in vaccines
made by Moderna and Pfizer/BioNTech.
In a
paper published in Nature Communications
, the researchers have shown for the first time that mRNA can be delivered into the cells where HIV is hiding, by encasing it in a tiny, specially formulated fat bubble. The mRNA then instructs the cells to reveal the virus.
Globally, there are
almost 40 million people
living with HIV, who must take medication for the rest of their lives in order to suppress the virus and ensure they do not develop symptoms or transmit it. For many it remains deadly, with UNAids figures suggesting one person died of HIV every minute in 2023.
It was “previously thought impossible” to deliver mRNA to the type of white blood cell that is home to HIV, said Dr Paula Cevaal, research fellow at the Doherty Institute and co-first author of the study, because those cells did not take up the fat bubbles, or lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), used to carry it.
The team have developed a new type of LNP that those cells will accept, known as LNP X. She said: “Our hope is that this new nanoparticle design could be a new pathway to an HIV cure.”
When a colleague first presented test results at the lab’s weekly meeting, Cevaal said, they seemed too good to be true.
“We sent her back into the lab to repeat it, and she came back the next week with results that were equally good. So we had to believe it. And of course, since then, we’ve repeated it many, many, many more times.
“We were overwhelmed by how [much of a] night and day difference it was – from not working before, and then all of a sudden it was working. And all of us were just sitting gasping like, ‘wow’.”
Further research will be needed to determine whether revealing the virus is enough to allow the body’s immune system to deal with it, or whether the technology will need to be combined with other therapies to eliminate HIV from the body.
The study is laboratory based and was carried out in cells donated by HIV patients. The path to using the technology as part of a cure for patients is long, and would require successful tests in animals followed by safety trials in humans, likely to take years, before efficacy trials could even begin.
“In the field of biomedicine, many things eventually don’t make it into the clinic – that is the unfortunate truth; I don’t want to paint a prettier picture than what is the reality,” stressed Cevaal. “But in terms of specifically the field of HIV cure, we have never seen anything close to as good as what we are seeing, in terms of how well we are able to reveal this virus.
“So from that point of view, we’re very hopeful that we are also able to see this type of response in an animal, and that we could eventually do this in humans.”
Dr Michael Roche of the University of Melbourne and co-senior author of the research, said the discovery could have broader implications beyond HIV, with the relevant white blood cells also involved in other diseases including cancers.
Dr Jonathan Stoye, a retrovirologist and emeritus scientist at the Francis Crick Institute, who was not involved in the study, said the approach taken by the Melbourne team appeared be a major advance on existing strategies to force the virus out of hiding, but further studies would be needed to determine how best to kill it after that.
He added: “Ultimately, one big unknown remains. Do you need to eliminate the entire reservoir for success or just the major part? If just 10% of the latent reservoir survives will that be sufficient to seed new infection? Only time will

data.title: Highly efficient matrix transpose in Mojo
data.author: timmyd
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用Mojo语言在Hopper架构上实现高效的矩阵转置内核。该内核实现了2775.49 GB/s的带宽，性能接近CUDA的2771.35 GB/s。文章详细描述了实现步骤，包括初始化TMA描述符、加载数据到共享内存、执行转置计算、以及将结果存储回全局内存。

主要步骤如下：

1. **初始化TMA描述符**：创建两个描述符，分别对应原始矩阵和转置矩阵。
2. **加载到共享内存**：使用TMA将数据异步复制到共享内存。
3. **计算转置**：在共享内存中完成矩阵转置。
4. **存储到GMEM**：将转置结果存储回全局内存。
5. **Swizzling优化**：通过调整描述符和索引实现进一步优化。

文章还提到，Mojo通过使用PTX API实现了比CUDA更高的带宽。Swizzling技术也被提及，提供了相关代码示例和详细解释的链接。最终的内核在性能上媲美CUDA，展示了Mojo在GPU计算上的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mojo编程语言及其在实际应用中的效果和局限性

不同观点：
• daft_pink认为Mojo因其封闭性和以盈利为目的的特性而受到限制，尤其是在2025年使用授权编程语言是不切实际的。
• olaf对Python兼容性优先考虑表示不满，特别是‘let’被移除，认为这是很大的缺点。
• sestep质疑矩阵转置的实际意义，认为转置应与其他操作融合以提高效率，而非单独进行。
• saagarjha对Mojo使用PTX API实现高速带宽表示怀疑，认为在Hopper架构上无需使用TMA即可达到相同效果。
• londons_explore与almostgotcaught持相似观点，认为矩阵转置应与其他操作结合，而不是单独实现。
• totalperspectiv关注代码大小问题，特别是在使用@parameter-for时是否会导致代码膨胀。
• iandanforth对图形表示的准确性提出疑问，认为图形中向量的方向可能有误。
• arjvik和jsnell对文章标题中声称的14%性能提升表示质疑，指出实际提升仅为0.14%。
• melodyogonna对不使用Modular提供的高层次抽象表示疑问。
• vlan121强烈反对Mojo编译器封闭源码的做法。
• thunkingdeep对文中使用的术语"archive"表示困惑，不确定是否为"achieve"之误。
• colesantiago询问Mojo在生产环境中的使用情况及招聘需求。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到矩阵转置是否应与其他操作结合以提高效率，这是技术实现上的一个争议点。
• Mojo的封闭性和编译器封闭源码问题引起了一些开发者的不满和质疑。
• 对性能提升数据的真实性和表述准确性存在争议，特别是标题中夸大的14%性能提升。
• 对Python兼容性和语法变更的讨论反映了开发者对语言设计方向的不同看法。
• 对高层次抽象的使用和编译器性能的技术细节也有一定关注。

44201527.article_content:
You've most likely heard about
gradient noise
through the name
Perlin
noise
, which refers to one particular implementation with various CPU
optimizations. Because it's an incredible tool for creative work, it's used
virtually everywhere: visual effects, video games, procedural mathematical art,
etc. While getting it right can sometimes be subtle, a "broken" implementation
can still look good or interesting. After all, "it looks fine, and I'm an
artist".
In order to gain a deeper and more meaningful understanding we will start
studying the 1D version (a case often omitted in the literature), then slowly
climb our way up in dimensions and complexity. We'll also work from a GPU
perspective rather than a CPU-based one, hence all code snippets and visuals
here are implemented in WebGL2/GLSL (hopefully without being too heavy on
performance). They should run on most modern devices; let me know if you run
into issues.
Before we begin, credit where it's due: most of the material here are nothing
new. This article is the result of weeks of studying and experimenting with
the maths from
Inigo Quilez's incredible pages
and other scattered
resources over the Internet. But as rich and valuable these resources are, they
sometimes move quickly over the details, assuming they're obvious. This post is
an attempt to fill those gaps.
A welcoming wavy 1D gradient noise signal
Hashing function and pseudo-random values
At the most elementary level, we need a deterministic coordinate based
pseudo-random system. More specifically, for any given integer coordinate we
need a random value, and as uniformly distributed as possible. Something like:
\begin{aligned}
h(-3) &= -0.006124 \\
h(-2) &= -0.996686 \\
h(-1) &= 0.200864 \\
h(0) &= -1.000000 \\
h(1) &= 0.053313 \\
h(2) &= -0.893312 \\
h(3) &= 0.854923 \\
\text{...}
\end{aligned}
Perlin's implementation relies on a permutation table, which is convenient when
working on the CPU, but more awkward for a shader. On the GPU, most people rely
on various floating point hacks or sub-optimal bit tricks, which often fall
short when exploring the full 32-bit range of inputs.
Note
We can not use a PRNG because it relies on a state where we need determinism
(for one coordinate, we always want the same random value). LCG (Linear
Congruential Generator) are a sub-classes of PRNG where the state is
actually the returned value. But even then, we can not re-use the previously
returned value since we need seeking; that is the ability to get the random
value associated with our integer coordinate. Trying to feed a PRNG/LCG with
our coordinate instead of the expected state would be equivalent to changing
the seed at every call, and this may create an important bias in the random
distribution. This is the reason why we need integer hashing instead.
So we need a hashing function, and we will have to limit ourselves to
32-bit because we're on the GPU. Fortunately, we won't have to look for
very long because in 2018
Chris Wellons found a pretty good one he named
lowbias32
, which was later
refined by TheIronBorn
.
This is the first building block we will be using, the hashing function:
uint hash(uint x) {
x = (x ^ (x >> 16)) * 0x21f0aaadU;
x = (x ^ (x >> 15)) * 0x735a2d97U;
return x ^ (x >> 15);
}
This is sweet and all, but a 32-bit unsigned integer is not directly useful by
itself, we need a normalized float. We could naively divide by
0xffffffff
,
but we'll end up with a nonuniform distribution (this is not as important as it
may sound to be honest). Instead, we will adapt the
technique presented by
Vigna Sebastiano for doubles
to floats, and in GLSL:
float u2f(uint x) { return float(x >> 8U) * uintBitsToFloat(0x33800000U); }
Combining these two functions into
u2f(hash(x))
maps any 32-bit
coordinate
x
to a random float in
[0,1)
.
To match our
h(x)
function from earlier and make it more "signal-like", we can
optionally center it around
0
by remapping it from
[0,1)
to
[-1,1)
:
h(x)=u2f(hash(x))*2.0-1.0
.
Expanding the hash function to more dimensions
When we will work in 2 or more dimensions, our input grid coordinates will be
more than one value, but we need a way to feed them to our single parameter hash
function. One trick is to use nested xor hash:
uint hash(uvec2 x) { return hash(x.x ^ hash(x.y)); }  // for 2D input
uint hash(uvec3 x) { return hash(x.x ^ hash(x.yz)); } // for 3D input
Using the pixel coordinates as input, we can test the hashing function in 2D:
float stepnoise2(vec2 p) {
ivec2 i = ivec2(floor(p));    // integer coordinate, or lattice
return u2f(hash(uvec2(i)));   // non-centered h(x)
}
Display h(x,y) by stepping the contiguous coordinates
Warning
We're going through an intermediate signed integer conversion before going
to unsigned to avoid issues with negative coordinates. Quoting GLSL 4.60
specifications: "It is undefined to convert a negative floating-point value
to an uint". With this conversion we will only have a problem when the
coordinates go outside the signed 32-bit range.
B

data.title: Why are smokestacks so tall?
data.author: azeemba
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了工业排放、空气污染控制以及烟囱在其中的作用。文章开头引用库尔特·冯内古特的一篇短篇小说，描绘了一个未实现的反乌托邦未来。人类自发现火以来，一直在权衡取暖和烹饪的好处与污染的危害。尽管我们希望生活在一个无排放的世界，但现实是许多工业过程都会产生污染物。

文章介绍了控制空气污染的技术，如催化反应器、静电除尘器和洗涤器，用于在污染物释放前进行处理。然而，并非所有污染物都能完全去除，因此在某些情况下，采取稀释和扩散策略以减少对健康的影响。烟囱通过提高排放高度，使污染物在高空分散，从而降低地面浓度。

虽然加热排放物以增加其上升能力可以促进扩散，但这会降低热效率。因此，烟囱设计需在污染控制和能量利用之间取得平衡。文章通过比萨烤炉演示了热空气上升的原理，并强调了烟囱在实际工程中的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：烟囱高度及其设计原因，包括传统原因和现代应用，以及与污染扩散和政治决策的关系。

不同观点：
• owenversteeg：传统上，更高的烟囱通过产生更大的 draft（抽力）来帮助炉子设计，因为更高的热空气柱会产生更大的压力差。现代虽然有了机械诱导的 draft，但高烟囱仍用于扩散污染物，因为高空风速更大，可以更广泛地分散污染物。
• rkagerer：简要解释了 draft 和高烟囱的作用，并提供了一个更易懂的解释链接。
• h1fra：认为该讨论让人对原本不感兴趣的话题产生兴趣，最终感到惊讶。
• a3w：提到高烟囱的政治背景，例如德国为减少本地植物死亡而加高烟囱，后来又引入过滤器。还提到气候变化使过滤器解决方案也不再完全有效。
• mcthorogood：指出在美国，烟囱高度的计算是为了不违反《清洁空气法》中的国家空气质量标准。
• saagarjha：猜测高烟囱是因为高空的风速更快，产生低压，从而抽起空气。
• ErrorNoBrain：认为高烟囱是为了不让工厂和周围区域被烟雾覆盖。
• pfdietz：提到了一种利用冷却空气产生下沉气流的技术，曾在洛杉矶被提议用于发电和净化空气，但因成本过高未实现。
• nemo44x：提到在建造烧烤炉时，更高的烟囱能产生更好的对流和烹饪效果。
• einpoklum：总结为高烟囱是为了确保污染物被充分扩散，减少对周围人的影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于高烟囱的主要功能是产生draft还是扩散污染物。传统观点侧重于draft的作用，而现代更多讨论其在污染物扩散中的作用。
• 政治和历史背景也被提及，特别是在环境保护政策变化下高烟囱的应用和调整。
• 不同应用场景（如工业烟囱、烧烤炉烟囱）下的烟囱设计和功能也被比较。

[Note that this article is a transcript of the video embedded above.]
“The big black stacks of the Illium Works of the Federal Apparatus Corporation spewed acid fumes and soot over the hundreds of men and women who were lined up before the red-brick employment office.” That’s the first line of one of my favorite short stories, written by Kurt Vonnegut in 1955. It paints a picture of a dystopian future that, thankfully, didn’t really come to be, in part because of those stacks.
In some ways, air pollution is kind of a part of life. I’d love to live in a world where the systems, materials and processes that make my life possible didn’t come with any emissions, but it’s just not the case... From the time that humans discovered fire, we’ve been methodically calculating the benefits of warmth, comfort, and cooking against the disadvantages of carbon monoxide exposure and particulate matter less than 2.5 microns in diameter… Maybe not in that exact framework, but basically, since the dawn of humanity, we’ve had to deal with smoke one way or another.
Since, we can’t accomplish much without putting unwanted stuff into the air, the next best thing is to manage how and where it happens to try and minimize its impact on public health. Of course, any time you have a balancing act between technical issues, the engineers get involved, not so much to help decide where to draw the line, but to develop systems that can stay below it. And that’s where the smokestack comes in. Its function probably seems obvious; you might have a chimney in your house that does a similar job. But I want to give you a peek behind the curtain into the Illium Works of the Federal Apparatus Corporation of today and show you what goes into engineering one of these stacks at a large industrial facility. I’m Grady, and this is Practical Engineering.
We put a lot of bad stuff in the air, and in a lot of different ways. There are roughly 200 regulated hazardous air pollutants in the United States, many with names I can barely pronounce. In many cases, the industries that would release these contaminants are required to deal with them at the source. A wide range of control technologies are put into place to clean dangerous pollutants from the air before it’s released into the environment. One example is coal-fired power plants. Coal, in particular, releases a plethora of pollutants when combusted, so, in many countries, modern plants are required to install control systems. Catalytic reactors remove nitrous oxides. Electrostatic precipitators collect particulates. Scrubbers use lime (the mineral, not the fruit) to strip away sulfur dioxide. And I could go on. In some cases, emission control systems can represent a significant proportion of the costs involved in building and operating a plant. But these primary emission controls aren’t always feasible for every pollutant, at least not for 100 percent removal.
There’s a very old saying that “the solution to pollution is dilution.” It’s not really true on a global scale. Case in point: There’s no way to dilute the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, or rather, it’s already as dilute as it’s going to get. But, it can be true on a local scale. Many pollutants that affect human health and the environment are short-lived; they chemically react or decompose in the atmosphere over time instead of accumulating indefinitely. And, for a lot of chemicals, there are concentration thresholds below which the consequences on human health are negligible. In those cases, dilution, or really dispersion, is a sound strategy to reduce their negative impacts, and so, in some cases, that’s what we do, particularly at major point sources like factories and power plants.
One of the tricks to dispersion is that many plumes are naturally buoyant. Naturally, I’m going to use my pizza oven to demonstrate this. Not all, but most pollutants we care about are a result of combustion; burning stuff up. So the plume is usually hot. We know hot air is less dense, so it naturally rises. And the hotter it is, the faster that happens. You can see when I first start the fire, there’s not much air movement. But as the fire gets hotter in the oven, the plume speeds up, ultimately rising higher into the air. That’s the whole goal: get the plume high above populated areas where the pollutants can be dispersed to a minimally-harmful concentration. It sounds like a simple solution - just run our boilers and furnaces super hot to get enough buoyancy for the combustion products to disperse.
The problem with the solution is that the whole reason we combust things is usually to recover the heat. So if you’re sending a lot of that heat out of the system, just because it makes the plume disperse better, you’re losing thermodynamic efficiency. It’s wasteful. That’s where the stack comes in. • nemo44x：提到在建造烧烤炉时，更高的烟囱能产生更好的对流和烹饪效果。
• einpoklum：总结为高烟囱是为了确保污染物被充分扩散，减少对周围人的影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于高烟囱的主要功能是产生draft还是扩散污染物。传统观点侧重于draft的作用，而现代更多讨论其在污染物扩散中的作用。
• 政治和历史背景也被提及，特别是在环境保护政策变化下高烟囱的应用和调整。
• 不同应用场景（如工业烟囱、烧烤炉烟囱）下的烟囱设计和功能也被比较。

data.title: Low-Level Optimization with Zig
data.author: Retro_Dev
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了程序优化的重要性及其在现代技术中的持续需求，特别是在使用Zig语言时的低级优化。作者指出，尽管编译器技术已有很大进步，但仍需开发者提供更多信息以帮助编译器生成更高效的代码。低级语言如Zig因其语法详尽，允许开发者传递更多细节信息，如对齐、别名需求、数组大小和元素类型，使编译器能生成更优质的代码。Zig的 verbosity、内置函数、非可选指针和comptime特性，使得开发者能更轻松地编写高性能程序。然而，Zig也存在一些权衡，例如需要手动指定非别名参数，否则Rust等语言可能表现更优。作者鼓励开发者理解编译器行为，以优化程序性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言的性能、编译时功能、语言设计与未来维护、编译器优化、语法设计等技术细节和选择标准。

不同观点：
• WalterBright认为Zig的comptime特性对其他编程语言有积极影响，比如D语言早在2007年引入了类似功能，并促进了其他语言的采纳。他同时指出Rust的内存模型在参数不别名的情况下提供了优化，而Zig需要手动指定。
• dustbunny作为游戏开发者，更关注构建系统、跨平台编译、迭代速度等特性，而不是纯粹的性能。他认为Zig在未来维护和模块化方面可能比C/C++更有优势。
• el_pollo_diablo则讨论了编译器在处理循环终止时的行为，并引用C11标准为Clang的行为辩护，认为编译器在此情况下没有违反语言规范。
• uecker反驳了comptime在字符串比较中不可或缺的观点，指出C语言也可以实现类似的内联和展开功能。
• csjh质疑高层次语言是否真的缺乏表达意图的能力，认为这与语言的高低层次无关。
• saagarjha不同意将Zig/Rust与V8引擎下的JavaScript直接对比，认为V8的优化方式不同，且现代语言大多可以进行类似的优化。
• kamma4434以Lisp的经验说明宏的优缺点，认为最好的宏是不需要写的，且它们在组合性上存在问题。
• KingOfCoders赞赏Zig的分配器模型，并希望在Go语言中也能使用类似的请求分配器，而非GC。
• flohofwoe喜欢Zig的详细语法，但认为它在某些方面过于繁琐，特别是在整数转换方面。他还指出Zig与C在编译优化上的差异主要来源于编译设置的不同。
• 9d指出某些语言特性更难优化，选择合适的语言能更快速和优雅地表达概念。
• timewizard批评现代语言添加过多"魔法"语法和符号，认为这不利于长时间阅读和维护。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Zig的comptime特性是否真的比其他语言（如C/C++、Rust）更具优势，特别是在编译时函数执行和优化方面。
• 另一个争议点是编译器优化设置对性能的影响，例如Zig和C在默认编译设置上的差异如何导致性能的不同。
• 语法设计的简洁性和可读性也被提出，部分开发者对现代语言中增加的符号和"魔法"语法表示不满。
• 游戏开发者特别关注语言和框架的未来维护和模块化能力，C/C++的长期主导地位受到Zig等新语言的挑战。

2025-06-07 # Optimizations with Zig
"Beware of the
Turing tar-pit
in which everything is possibile, but nothing of interest is easy." - Alan Perlis 1982
What is of interest to you? Many things, I am certain. One such topic that I am constantly intrigued by
is program optimization. Whether you are looking to
compute the largest fibonacci number
in one second, or creating the
fastest financial transaction database
ever
written, or even just
rewriting something in rust
, you likely know how rewarding optimization can be.
Optimization separates the weak from the fast. Optimization isn't a thing of the past. Advances in
technology shape the form of our programs, but don't negate the need to optimize. Well optimized
programs save money, enable higher-tier scaling opportunities, and preserve system simplicity. Would you
rather spend thousands to run shoddy code on autoscaling cloud infrastructure, or write better code,
letting you use a handful of mid-tier servers at reduced latency and cost?
In this article I aim to explain the concept of low-level optimization, and why Zig is particularly well
suited for it. If you enjoy what you read, please consider
supporting me
:)
Trust the compiler?
Some people would say "trust the compiler, it knows best." It sure does, for most low-level situations!
Optimizing compilers have come a long ways. Increased system resources and
advances in IR transformations
have
enabled compiler backends like
LLVM
to deliver
impressive results
.
Compilers are complicated beasts. The best optimizing backends will still
generate sub
-
par code
in some cases. In fact, even
state-of-art compilers will
break language
specifications
(
Clang assumes
that all loops without side effects will terminate). It is up to
us to give our compilers as much information as possible, and verify that the compiler is functioning
correctly. In the case of most low-level languages, you can generally massage your code until the
compiler realizes it can apply a certain transform. In other situations, it's not so easy.
Why are low-level languages generally more performant? You might think the reason is that high level
languages are doing a lot of extra work, such as garbage collection, string interning, interpreting
code, etc. While you are right, this isn't *entirely* complete. High level languages lack something that
low level languages have in great adundance - intent.
The verbosity of low level programming languages enable us to produce code that the compiler can reason
about very well. As an example, consider the following JavaScript code:
function maxArray(x, y) {
for (let i = 0; i < 65536; i++) {
x[i] = y[i] > x[i] ? y[i] : x[i];
}
}
As humans, we can interpret this code as setting the values in
x
as the maximum of
x
and
y
. The
generated bytecode
for this JavaScript (under V8) is pretty bloated. As a
comparison, here is what the function might look like if it were written in Zig:
fn maxArray(
noalias x: *align(64) [65536]f64,
y: *align(64) const [65536]f64,
) void {
for (x, y, 0..) |a, b, i| {
x[i] = if (b > a) b else a;
}
}
In this more verbose language, we can tell the compiler additional information about our code. For
example, the optimizer now knows about alignment, aliasing requirements, array sizes, and array element
types - all at compile-time. Using this information, the compiler generates
far superior, even vectorized
code.
If you were wondering,
equivalent Rust
code
generates near identical assembly.
So can we *really* trust our compilers? It depends. Are you looking to uncover transformations to triple
the throughput of your program's performance bottleneck? You should probably look at what the compiler
is doing, and figure out if there are better ways to express *your intent* to the compiler. You may need
to tweak the code to get the transforms you want. In the worst cases, you may discover that the compiler
isn't applying optimal transforms to your code. In these cases, you may need to write inline assembly to
squeeze out that last drop.
But what about high level code? Except for
niche
cases
, the most we can do is
reason about loops
. In other words, compilers cannot change our algorithms and
optimize our paradigms. Their scope is relatively narrow.
So where does Zig fall?
I love Zig for it's verbosity. Due to this verbosity, it's easier to write more performant programs than
with most other languages. With Zig's
builtin
functions
, non-optional
pointers
,
unreachable
keyword
, well chosen
illegal
behavior
, Zig's excellent
comptime
... LLVM is practically spoon-fed information about our code.
It isn't all rainbows though, there are tradeoffs. For example, Rust's memory model allows the compiler
to always assume that function arguments never alias. You must manually specify this in Zig. If the
compiler can't tell that your Zig function is always called with non-aliasing arguments, Rust
functions will outperform the non-annotated Zig functions.
If we take in well-annotated LLVM IR as the *only* met

data.title: Windows 10 spies on your use of System Settings (2021)
data.author: userbinator
data.article_summary: 本文作者Michael Horowitz指出，Windows 10在其系统设置中存在监控用户行为的现象。作者使用Nir Sofer的工具DNSLookupView和TcpLogView进行测试，发现每当查看系统设置时，操作系统会生成对www.bing.com和cxcs.microsoft.net的DNS查询和数据传输请求。尽管数据通过HTTPS加密，无法直接查看内容，但作者猜测这可能与微软的客户体验计划有关。作者建议用户可以通过阻止相关域名（如cxcs.microsoft.net）来减少此类监控行为，并强调Bing不仅仅是搜索引擎，还可能用于 telemetry（遥测数据传输）。作者呼吁用户采取防御性措施，如修改路由器设置以保护隐私。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows系统的数据收集和隐私问题

不同观点：
• **JdeBP的观点**：认为所谓的"telemetry"并非在向微软报告用户数据，而是在从微软获取信息并展示给用户。他通过分析版本号和更新日期，指出这些数据是与微软下载内容的更新相关，而非用户行为的报告。

• **callamdelaney的观点**：认为Windows 10和11都在监视用户行为，例如Windows照片应用会分析图片并可能将数据报告给微软。他引用Reddit上的讨论来支持其观点，认为多个应用都在进行深度数据收集。

• **Sophira的观点**：讨论了通过hosts文件阻止域名的困难，指出一些程序会绕过hosts文件直接查询公共DNS。他还提到微软可能通过硬编码IP地址绕过DNS封锁，使得完全阻止连接变得困难。

• **globalnode的观点**：将Windows描述为广告/间谍软件，认为用户对其计算机的控制权有限。他建议在没有互联网连接的情况下使用计算机以避免数据收集。

• **eurekin的观点**：对版本号的意义提出疑问，并认为即使是简单的"关于"对话框也可能需要调用服务器来检查软件的最新版本。

• **cosmotic的观点**：怀念以前控制面板的功能明确且帮助文档本地化的时代，现在设置按钮经常打开Bing搜索结果页面，且结果为零。

• **butz的观点**：猜测微软可能会利用收集的遥测数据来创建第三个"控制面板"。

• **userbinator的观点**：观察到Windows 11也存在类似问题，认为越来越难让Windows在网络上保持安静，许多软件都有后台网络活动。

• **red_admiral的观点**：认为标准遥测数据可能是用于聚合分析，且数据是匿名化的。虽然不理想，但对个人隐私影响不大。

• **nmeofthestate的观点**：认为需要对网络请求和响应内容进行调查以了解实际情况，而不是仅凭猜测指责间谍行为。

• **barrkel的观点**：指出遥测的通常目的是了解用户使用哪些功能，以指导产品开发和功能取舍。

• **alkonaut的观点**：质疑用户为何不愿让厂商看到其访问的设置页面，认为如果用户选择退出遥测就不应发送数据，但承认必要和可选网络调用的界限模糊。

• **NitpickLawyer的观点**：分享了Android设备上的类似经历，认为在理想情况下应有选项来接受或拒绝收集的数据。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如Devasta和qwertox）表达了对微软操作系统的失望，认为其在功能和用户体验上不如从前，且可能进行更广泛的数据收集。
• 争议的焦点在于Windows系统是否在未经用户同意的情况下收集和报告用户数据，以及这些数据的具体用途和隐私影响。
• 用户对微软通过系统设置界面和后台网络活动进行数据收集的方式表示担忧，并质疑其透明度和控制选项的有效性。

Michael Horowitz
Home
=>  Windows 10 spies on your use of System Settings
When printed, this page will be automatically re-formatted.
There are no separate "Printer Friendly" versions of pages on this site.
To preview the printed format, use Print Preview in your browser.
[Formatted for Printing]
From the personal web site of
Michael Horowitz
Windows 10 spies on your use of System Settings
Microsoft knows you did this
October 23, 2021
I am a big fan of Nir Sofer. He creates
great utilities
for Windows and his software is both free and portable. Recently, he released a new DNS logging program
DNSLookupView
.
He already had a DNS logging program called
DNSQuerySniffer
but the new program gets its raw data from a different source.
So, I have been running both of them side by side to see the pros/cons of each.
And, while logging DNS requests on a Windows 10 machine, I came across some interesting stuff. The computer in question was running Windows 10 Home Edition, service pack 20H2, build 19042.1083, which means it has bug fixes as of July 6, 2021. It was logged on with a local account, not a Microsoft account. It was also locked down as much as possible. Every customization I could find in the Systems Settings was disabled. Many of the  scheduled telemetry tasks were disabled.
With the DNS logging programs running, I happened to look at the System Settings.
I didn't
change
anything, just
looked
at a couple settings.
DNSLookupView showed that this generated two DNS queries, one for
www.bing.com
and another for
cxcs.microsoft.net
. If you are thinking WTF? So was I. You can see the DNS log below.
DNSLookupView output
The queries were made by program
C:\Windows\ImmersiveControlPanel\SystemSettings.exe
and the query type was AAAA. The sub-domain
www.bing.com
resolved to ::ffff:13.107.21.200 and  ::ffff:204.79.197.200.
The sub-domain
cxcs.microsoft.net
resolved to ::ffff:96.17.141.116.
Of course a DNS query is not data transmission. Typically, however, it immediately precedes a data transmission.
After seeing this the first time, I ran a second test that looked for data transmission. For this, I used another Nir Sofer program called
TcpLogView
that logs every outbound TCP request. If Windows is phoning home via UDP, I would not see it.
Below is the output from TCPLogView for the exact same second (2:30 and 51 seconds) as the DNS queries  for
www.bing.com
and
cxcs.microsoft.net
.
TCPLogView showing outbound requests
We see that program
C:\Windows\ImmersiveControlPanel\SystemSettings.exe
made two outbound requests.
The first was to port 443 (HTTPS) at IP address
13.107.21.200
which is
www.bing.com
.
The second was to port 443 at IP address
96.17.141.116
which is
cxcs.microsoft.net
. Twenty seconds after opening a socket to these two computers,
SystemSettings.exe
closed the socket.
Clearly Windows 10 spies on you any time you use the System Settings
.
What else are they spying on?
What I did is quite repeatable, feel free to try it yourself.
NOTE: I did not log the actual data being transmitted between my computer and Microsoft. Since it went to the HTTPS port (443) it was surely encrypted.
I wondered what
cxcs.microsoft.net
is. When I viewed the site in a browser, it returned
2021.1019.1.0
, whatever that means. It was not even HTML, just plain text. A search for the sub-domain turned up a
guess
that it might be the Microsoft customer experience center. There is/was a
Microsoft Customer Experience Center
that went by CXC. I also found it on a  list of domains to be
blocked
by AdGuard or PiHole.
As for
www.bing.com
, it clearly is doing double duty. More than just a search engine, it seems to be used for telemetry too.
BLOCKING CXCS.MICROSOFT.NET
The first thing I did was block access to
cxcs.microsoft.net
(more on this below). Then, I ran the above test again to make sure that I could still use the System Settings app. And, another interesting thing turned up.
The System Settings worked without access to
cxcs.microsoft.net
, but in testing, I saw another DNS request, this time to
ctldl.windowsupdate.com
. I tested it twice and each time program SystemSettings.exe made DNS requests for
www.bing.com
and
ctldl.windowsupdate.com
. I had already blocked the Windows Update website so the only outbound request it could make was to Bing.
The next day, I tested again and the result is shown below.
More DNS Queries the next day
This time, program SystemSettings.exe tried to resolve all three servers. Two of them resolved to IP address zero thanks to my router. It made the one outbound TCP request that it could, to
www.bing.com
at 13.107.21.200 (port 443). My testing of the Settings app was very quick. I have to wonder if I looked at many different settings and actually changed a setting or two what other servers Windows would try to phone home to.
Clearly Bing is more than a search engine. It seems to be spying on us.

• **JdeBP的观点**：认为所谓的"telemetry"并非在向微软报告用户数据，而是在从微软获取信息并展示给用户。他通过分析版本号和更新日期，指出这些数据是与微软下载内容的更新相关，而非用户行为的报告。

• **callamdelaney的观点**：认为Windows 10和11都在监视用户行为，例如Windows照片应用会分析图片并可能将数据报告给微软。他引用Reddit上的讨论来支持其观点，认为多个应用都在进行深度数据收集。

• **Sophira的观点**：讨论了通过hosts文件阻止域名的困难，指出一些程序会绕过hosts文件直接查询公共DNS。他还提到微软可能通过硬编码IP地址绕过DNS封锁，使得完全阻止连接变得困难。

• **globalnode的观点**：将Windows描述为广告/间谍软件，认为用户对其计算机的控制权有限。他建议在没有互联网连接的情况下使用计算机以避免数据收集。

• **eurekin的观点**：对版本号的意义提出疑问，并认为即使是简单的"关于"对话框也可能需要调用服务器来检查软件的最新版本。

• **cosmotic的观点**：怀念以前控制面板的功能明确且帮助文档本地化的时代，现在设置按钮经常打开Bing搜索结果页面，且结果为零。

• **butz的观点**：猜测微软可能会利用收集的遥测数据来创建第三个"控制面板"。

• **userbinator的观点**：观察到Windows 11也存在类似问题，认为越来越难让Windows在网络上保持安静，许多软件都有后台网络活动。

• **red_admiral的观点**：认为标准遥测数据可能是用于聚合分析，且数据是匿名化的。虽然不理想，但对个人隐私影响不大。

• **nmeofthestate的观点**：认为需要对网络请求和响应内容进行调查以了解实际情况，而不是仅凭猜测指责间谍行为。

• **barrkel的观点**：指出遥测的通常目的是了解用户使用哪些功能，以指导产品开发和功能取舍。

• **alkonaut的观点**：质疑用户为何不愿让厂商看到其访问的设置页面，认为如果用户选择退出遥测就不应发送数据，但承认必要和可选网络调用的界限模糊。

• **NitpickLawyer的观点**：分享了Android设备上的类似经历，认为在理想情况下应有选项来接受或拒绝收集的数据。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如Devasta和qwertox）表达了对微软操作系统的失望，认为其在功能和用户体验上不如从前，且可能进行更广泛的数据收集。
• 争议的焦点在于Windows系统是否在未经用户同意的情况下收集和报告用户数据，以及这些数据的具体用途和隐私影响。
• 用户对微软通过系统设置界面和后台网络活动进行数据收集的方式表示担忧，并质疑其透明度和控制选项的有效性。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何通过逆向工程优化Cursor的大语言模型（LLM）客户端。作者团队使用TensorZero框架在Cursor和LLM之间建立连接，以观察和优化API调用。他们通过设置反向代理和Nginx解决连接问题，并处理了CORS认证，最终成功实现了对Cursor的观测和实验优化。这项工作使得工程师可以根据生产指标、用户反馈和行为数据对Cursor进行个性化调整，并进一步优化提示词和模型。后续文章将介绍如何收集反馈并完成优化循环。

44207063.article_content:
Reverse Engineering Cursor's LLM Client
June 5, 2025
· Viraj Mehta, Aaron Hill, Gabriel Bianconi
What happens under the hood at Cursor?
We wired
TensorZero
between Cursor and the LLMs to see every token fly by… and bend those API calls to our own will.
TensorZero is an open-source framework that helps engineers optimize LLM applications with downstream feedback signals (e.g. production metrics, human feedback, user behavior), and we figured it would be interesting to see whether we could use TensorZero on the LLM application we use most heavily ourselves: Cursor.
With our gateway between Cursor and the LLM providers, we can observe the LLM calls being made, run evaluations on individual inferences, use inference-time optimizations, and even experiment with and optimize the prompts and models that Cursor uses.
Cursor is optimized for its population of users as a whole — beyond
.cursorrules
, is there room for improvement by diving deeper and tailoring it to individual users?
What would it look like to be able to empirically experiment with and optimize Cursor for your individual usage patterns?
Beyond optimization, Cursor still operates as a black box.
Wouldn’t it be interesting to see what’s actually being sent to the models?
Nearly all LLM optimization, evaluation, and experimentation techniques require data on what inferences were made and their real-world consequences.
In this post, we’ll focus on the former and dive into how we set up TensorZero as a self-hosted proxy between Cursor and the LLMs that it calls.
If you’d like to try it yourself, check out the
example
in our repository.
We’ll follow up with a blog post on how we collect feedback and close the optimization loop.
Wiring Things Together
The first thing we noticed was that Cursor lets you override the OpenAI base URL and model names.
Perfect.
TensorZero exposes an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint, so we can easily configure Cursor to call TensorZero instead of OpenAI.
In the TensorZero configuration, we define a TensorZero function
cursorzero
so that we can automatically experiment with different models and prompts while storing provider-agnostic inference and feedback data in our database for observability and optimization.
The First Roadblock: Cursor’s Servers
Cursor was initially unable to connect to TensorZero running locally.
It turns out that Cursor first sends a request to its own servers, where additional processing happens before making the LLM call, so it couldn’t connect to our gateway on
localhost
.
(This also means that your credentials must be forwarded to Cursor’s servers, allowing them to collect data on your inferences and codebase.)
As a test that our plan could work in the first place, we pointed Cursor to OpenRouter and realized we could use its models for the Ask, Agent, and Cmd+K interactions in Cursor.
We were also still able to use the normal Cursor Tab completions, which rely on a proprietary model Cursor serves for inline completions (it is very good, so we’re glad to be able to keep it).
The solution was to set up a reverse proxy to expose a public endpoint that would forward requests back to our machine.
We used Ngrok to keep things simple.
Since we were exposing a gateway with LLM credentials to the public Internet, we added Nginx in front of our gateway to authenticate requests.
We set Cursor’s base URL to our Ngrok endpoint, added the credentials we set up in Nginx, turned off built-in models, and finally added our new TensorZero function under the model name
tensorzero::function_name::cursorzero
.
In the end, the workflow looked like this: Cursor → Ngrok → Nginx (self-hosted) → TensorZero (self-hosted) → LLM providers
But it didn’t work.
The Second Roadblock: CORS
The authentication process had failed.
Nginx logs showed that there was an
OPTIONS
request hitting our endpoint, so we configured Nginx to return headers on
OPTIONS
requests and incrementally added headers we saw in responses from the OpenAI API.
This is the initial verification request that comes from the local Cursor IDE.
The CORS requirement likely comes from Electron.
After the initial verification, all requests come from Cursor’s servers.
Our Nginx Configuration to handle CORS headers
# --- CORS helper macro ---
set $CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN  $http_origin;   # reflect the caller's origin
set $CORS_ALLOW_HEADERS "Authorization,Content-Type";
location / {
# --- pre-flight ---
if ($request_method = OPTIONS) {
add_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin      $CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN always;
add_header Access-Control-Allow-Credentials "true"             always;
add_header Access-Control-Allow-Methods     "GET,POST,OPTIONS" always;
add_header Access-Control-Allow-Headers     $CORS_ALLOW_HEADERS always;
add_header Access-Control-Max-Age           86400              always;
return 204;  # 204 (No Content) is conventional for pre-flight
}
}
You can find the entire codebase for “CursorZero” on
GitHub
.
It finally worked!
Finally: Observability for Cursor
We could finally

data.title: A tool for burning visible pictures on a compact disc surface (2022)
data.author: carlesfe
data.article_summary:
CDImage 是一个用于在光盘表面刻录可见图片的工具。该项目受早期类似尝试的启发，特别是 Instructables 用户 argon 和昵称为 [unDEFER] 的开发者的工作。作者在颜色和光盘几何参数上进行了实验，并创建了一个带有视觉预览模式的图形用户界面。由于每种光盘的校准问题，作者在2008年放弃了该项目，但最近整理并分享了代码，以纪念光盘时代。

要构建该工具，需要 Qt 6 库。Windows用户也可以使用提供的二进制文件，但未经充分测试。使用时需加载高对比度图片，并选择光盘型号；若型号不在列表中，需手动输入几何参数，但校准困难且可能浪费光盘。刻录音轨需较长时间，最终生成一个约800MB的音频CD。建议使用 cdrecord 等工具刻录。校准过程涉及多目标优化问题，可能需要多次尝试和专业反馈。

CDImage
A tool for burning visible pictures on a compact disc surface
Project's Origins and Credits
I know of at least two successful attempts to implement a similar technique. One was accomplished about 15 years ago by
argon
Instructables user.
Another attempt
was made by a user with nickname [unDEFER] (no English documentation unfortunately). These two projects inspired me some time ago. And in fact my coordinate conversion code is mostly based on [unDEFER]’s implementation. I also used geometric parameters of some compact discs from that project. I acknowledge and am grateful to these developers for their contributions.
I played with color shades and different compact discs with moderate success and created a GUI with visual preview mode. I tried to implement a user-friendly solution but finally abandoned the project in 2008 due to a problem of calibration for every particular brand and type of compact disc. Recently I found my old code and decided to share it. More as a tribute to the compact disc era. But maybe you will make some use of it. I fixed some obvious bugs, brushed the code up a little and ported it to modern Qt6. I considered porting to Python but I still need C++ because audio track generation takes some time even on modern hardware.
Building
You'll need
Qt 6
library to build it. Just run
qmake
and then
make
. Alternatively you could build the project with
Qt Creator
if you installed it.
Windows Users
Since many Windows users experienced problems with building it or did not want to install Qt and all the stuff, I've made a
Windows binary build
.
However I have not tested it thoroughly yet because I don't have a working CD recorder at hand right now.
I think I'll try to burn some discs with Windows tools later and note down the steps for Windows users.
Before you start
If your compact disc is not mentioned in the track generating dialog, you'll probably fail. All the discs are slightly different geometrically. This difference does not matter for data storage but dramatically influences image calculation.
You could try to guess geometry of an unknown disc and input it manually, but you'll probably spoil a lot of discs before you get some results. Moreover, all your test discs should be perfectly identical or you should use the same CD-RW disc. Sometimes discs of the same model happen to have different parameters. Don't know why. After all, manufacturers have never cared since those discs were never supposed to be used this way.
Usage
Click
Edit→Load image
and select an image file. I recommend that you use a high-contrast image. If you choose a full color image, it will be converted to grayscale. You can adjust and scale your image:
left mouse button
— move image;
double click
— center image;
mouse scroll wheel
— zoom image.
Click Edit→Create track and select the model of your compact disc.
If your disc is not in the list (which is likely), you may input geometry manually. However unknown disc calibration is neither easy nor quick procedure. If you still wish to give it a try, I recommend that you read the
"Red Book"
as well as
Considering Calibration
section before you start.
If you know the geometry of some compact disc which is not in the list, let me know and I’ll include it into the distribution.
Depending on your hardware, conversion will take some time. Finally you’ll get a huge Audio CD track.
Yes, about 800Mb, which is normal for
Audio CD
.
You could use any software you like to burn it. For example:
cdrecord -audio dev=<recorder_device> <generated_track>
Remember that you should create an
Audio CD
!
Considering Calibration
From the Mathematical point of view we have a sort of
multi-objective optimization
problem. Bicriteria optimization, to be more precise. It means that two objective functions should be optimized simultaneously. If we define goal as getting a "neat image", we need an expert who is able to provide some feedback regarding image "quality". Which leads us to
interactive methods
.
The first and the most obvious idea is to select some series of equally spaced values for each criterium and burn a lot of discs with all possible combinations. If the space is narrow enough, you'll see something at some discs. Then narrow the range and repeat. A typical Computational Mathematics approach. A lot of iterations and time.

要构建该工具，需要 Qt 6 库。Windows用户也可以使用提供的二进制文件，但未经充分测试。使用时需加载高对比度图片，并选择光盘型号；若型号不在列表中，需手动输入几何参数，但校准困难且可能浪费光盘。刻录音轨需较长时间，最终生成一个约800MB的音频CD。建议使用 cdrecord 等工具刻录。校准过程涉及多目标优化问题，可能需要多次尝试和专业反馈。

• [Molitor5901] 提到了 LightScribe 技术，认为它也是一种很棒的技术，用于在光盘上刻录图像。

data.title: What was Radiant AI, anyway?
data.author: paavohtl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了《上古卷轴4：湮灭》中的**Radiant AI**技术，以及其在游戏社区中引发的长期争议和误解。Radiant AI本应为游戏中的NPC带来动态、智能的行为，使世界更加生动。然而，这一技术在2006年游戏发布时并未完全实现，导致玩家和开发者之间的长期讨论。文章详细分析了Radiant AI的承诺、实际表现及其在后续游戏如《辐射3》、《天际》和《星空》中的演变。作者通过研究论坛、早期杂志和模组工具，试图澄清对Radiant AI的误解，并指出其在Bethesda游戏历史中的重要性。文章还提到《湮灭重制版》的发布重新引发了对这些话题的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕游戏中NPC的人工智能（特别是Bethesda的"Radiant AI"技术）的实际表现、期望和潜在改进的讨论。

不同观点：
• **kibwen的观点**：指出Bethesda游戏中的AI存在一些未公开的、因Bug导致的问题，比如《Oblivion》中的skooma成瘾者因AI包和派系分配错误，无法进入小屋而永远停留在外面。这表明游戏AI在细节处理上存在缺陷。

• **flohofwoe的观点**：认为像Dwarf Fortress那样的完全由目标驱动的AI系统与故事驱动的游戏存在矛盾。前者是不可预测的，而后者需要故事结局是确定的且玩家是英雄。因此，完全不可预测的AI可能不适合有明确故事线的游戏。

• **nxobject的观点**：提出三个要素——足够有趣的任务NPC、具有涌现行为的模拟世界以及NPC不离开城镇——可能是不兼容的。这意味着一个具有高度AI互动的世界可能难以维持稳定的任务和剧情供应。

• **ednite的观点**：对现代AI与开放世界模拟结合的可能性表示期待，设想未来可能出现具有真正推理能力的NPC，并提出如《World of Warcraft》中的情景作为例子。

• **devstar的观点**：作为Bethesda粉丝，分享个人经验，指出在《Fallout 3》中观察到NPC获取玩家储存武器的行为，并认为这是对AI的一种突破，尽管可能与记忆混淆有关。

• **hyperman1的观点**：分享在《Gothic》中观察到的核心NPC自主参与战斗的经历，认为这是理想的AI行为，并期望"Radiant AI"能有类似的表现。

• **ajkjk的观点**：回顾"Radiant AI"在《Oblivion》宣传时的炒作与失望，但同时也保持对该技术可能实现的潜在期待。

• **YeGoblynQueenne的观点**：通过对比《Rain World》中的独立AI行为，指出玩家对非固定敌人位置的游戏机制的负面反应，并认为完全模拟独立AI的世界未必能被广泛接受。

• **dedicate的观点**：表示不希望NPC通过图灵测试，而是希望世界有活力，NPC能对世界做出反应，如因私人原因调整行为，而不是仅仅对玩家做出反应。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了AI技术在游戏中应用的现实与理想的差距，特别是Bethesda游戏中的"Radiant AI"技术的局限性和潜在改进方向。
• 不同玩家对AI的期望不同，有的希望看到更复杂的NPC互动，有的则对完全不可预测的AI持保留态度。
• 提到了《Rain World》作为独立AI行为的一个例子，并通过玩家反馈说明完全独立AI的游戏设计可能面临的挑战。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于AI的不可预测性和故事驱动游戏的确定性之间的矛盾，以及玩家对独立AI行为的接受程度。

Table of contents
Wake up, weâre here
What was promised
Announcement and cover story
The E3 2005 demo
Fan interviews and forum quotes
Radiant AI misbehavior and a mysterious quote
Release and reactions
So what was Radiant AI?
Character attributes

AI package schedules and conditions
Flags, location and target
How the world works, and low-level AI processing
A little more conversation
Radiant AI mythbusting
Claims from the announcement article and interviews
The E3 demo, revisited
The skooma incident
Mystery quote anecdotes
Radiant AI and GOAP
GOAP example
Radiant AI vs GOAP
GOAP in Fallout 3(?)
How Radiant AI changed before Oblivionâs release
Radiant AI after Oblivion
Fallout 3 and New Vegas
Skyrim and the rise of Radiant Story
Fallout 4
Starfield
Conclusion
The recent release of
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered
has rekindled the publicâs interest in the 19-year-old RPG classic, making it once again â at least temporarily â one of the most played and talked about Bethesda Game Studios titles. The remaster is a comprehensive upgrade of the original, featuring fully remade yet mostly faithful graphics, select gameplay improvements and a redesigned user interface. But it is still Oblivion, and I donât mean that in the sense that it âmaintains the spirit of the original gameâ or something like that. The remaster is quite literally built on top of the original game; the Oblivion from 2006, including its game engine and content, is still there, just with an Unreal Engine 5 wrapper handling the audio-visual side of things.
Unreal Engine 5 can produce mind-boggling effects.
And that is interesting because Oblivion was a very ambitious game for its time. The world was huge, the graphics were cutting edge, but perhaps more importantly, it promised to deliver a dynamic and living world, with over a thousand fully voice-acted non-player characters (NPCs). The technology powering this was called
Radiant AI
, but it was too ambitious for its time and was mostly cut from the final game. Or maybe it was used in Oblivion, but Bethesda gave up on it before shipping Fallout 3 and / or Skyrim. Or maybe it was never really there in the first place, and
Todd
lied to us all along. What was Radiant AI, anyway?
This is a topic Iâve seen discussed in online spaces for quite literally decades, and the Oblivion remaster has brought it back into the spotlight once again among the terminally online. People mostly know it as the original Bethesda controversy; one of the first times
BGS
promised something they ultimately couldnât deliver. However, very few people outside of the most hardcore fans and modders have even tried to understand it themselves. And by understanding, I mean the whole thing: why was it needed, what it was promised to be, what it actually was, and where it is now. This mammoth of an article (
looks nervously at the reading time estimate
) is my attempt to do just that.
This was supposed to be a short sidequest; a hopefully straightforward explanation of what Radiant AI is, and an opportunity to correct some of the popular misconceptions about it. But alas, things rarely are that simple. Iâve scoured through old RPG forums, fansites, modding tutorials and scans of early 2000s gaming magazines. Iâve spent maybe a couple dozen hours just exploring how Bethesda games work using their modding tools, from Morrowind to Starfield (which I had to buy just to check some facts). I even had to resort to reading the source code to the various script extender mods and DLL plugins â thatâs how scarce the information is. Still, I donât feel that Iâm the most qualified person to write about this, as experienced Bethesda modders would have known a lot of this already. It is almost guaranteed that I got something wrong, so please
@ me on Bluesky
or elsewhere with corrections.
You can use the table of contents to skip to the parts that interest you the most, or just read it all if you have the time. Every heading is an anchor link, so you can also bookmark or share specific sections. Happy reading.
But before we can get to Radiant AI, weâll have to go back to the island of Vvardenfell, where it all began. Well it didnât really begin there, but letâs talk about Morrowind first anyway.
Wake up, weâre here
Video games from Bethesda Game Studios are known for many things: large open worlds, huge modding communities, mediocre combat systems, and of course, bugs. The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind wasnât the first game in the series â hence the roman III in the title â but it established many of the conventions that would define
BGSFPRPGs
for the next two (and soon three) decades. It was the first game to be built with Bethesdaâs new game engine â a fork of Gamebryo, later rebranded as
Creation Engine
â which is still in use today, and brought the series into the hardware-accelerated 3D era. Morrowind pivoted from Daggerfallâs mostly procedurally generated world to a hand

data.title: Show HN: Ask-human-mcp – zero-config human-in-loop hatch to stop hallucinations
data.author: echollama
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI代理在遇到不确定问题时如何处理的讨论，包括技术解决方案、概念评价以及实际应用中的问题。

不同观点：
• superb_dev提到网站在手机上阅读体验差，左侧内容被裁剪且无法滚动，这涉及到用户体验和技术实现的问题。
• loloquwowndueo构想了一个“让人类作为服务”（human as a service）的场景，最终可能演变成机器之间的循环请求，反映了AI与人类互动中的潜在问题。
• threeseed认为MCP服务器可以让代理在不确定时请求人类帮助，但指出AI无法识别自己的错误或提供准确的信心评分，暗示这种方法的局限性。
• mgraczyk建议在光标规则中添加指令，让AI在不确定时请求用户帮助，提出了具体的实现方案。
• exclipy希望通过Slack或WhatsApp接收通知，以解决AI暂停等待的问题，涉及到用户通知机制的优化。
• PSBigBig对帖子内容表示感谢并进行了收藏，属于正面反馈。
• kjhughes质疑代理如何识别自己何时不确定或卡住，提出了技术实现中的关键问题。
• throwaway314155对“幻觉”（hallucination）定义提出疑问，并认为该概念简单而巧妙，暗示其潜在价值。
• kordlessagain提出通过创建“通用MCP工具”来解决现有工具不足的问题，提供了另一种技术实现思路。
• ddalex认为基于文档的AI可以比人类更快更好地回答问题，质疑人类在某些情况下的必要性。
• rgbrenner指出该概念与Roo中的`ask_followup_question`类似，提供了类比和参考。
• conception询问使用的具体提示语，涉及到具体实现细节。
• spacecadet建议在AI提供明显错误答案或幻觉时重新开始，强调用户输入的调整和优化。
• atoav分享了在大学实验室中因LLM提供的错误电子建议导致的问题，指出了LLM在实际应用中的局限性和潜在风险。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个技术实现细节，如MCP服务器、光标规则添加指令、通用MCP工具等，显示了不同解决方案的可行性。
• 对AI幻觉和不确定性的识别是争议焦点之一，反映了当前AI技术在处理不确定性时的局限。
• 实际应用中的问题，如atoav在电子实验室遇到的错误建议，强调了AI在专业领域应用中的风险和挑战。

data.article_summary: 2023年6月，唐纳德·特朗普与埃隆·马斯克之间的争执升级，主要围绕马斯克批评特朗普支持的预算协调法案，并在社交媒体上展开激烈交锋。特朗普威胁取消与马斯克公司（如SpaceX）的政府合同，马斯克则回应称将开始退役SpaceX的“龙”飞船。虽然双方言辞激烈，但并未落实为实际行动。马斯克随后收回了退役威胁。争执引发了对SpaceX可能失去NASA和国防部重要合同的担忧，因为这些机构高度依赖SpaceX的 launch services。与此同时，特朗普撤回了提名杰瑞德·艾萨克曼担任NASA局长的决定，称其为民主党人，不合适。总体而言，争执被视为言辞上的对峙，实际影响有限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特朗普与马斯克之间的冲突及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **onlyrealcuzzo**: 认为总统不应基于个人喜好或CEO是否称赞总统来决定政府合同的授予。这种做法类似于基于裙带关系，而非实际表现来分配资源，可能导致腐败，类似于导致苏联崩溃的路径。

• **thinkindie**: 将特朗普与柏 Berlusconi 对比，暗示美国现在也面临类似的问题，尤其是考虑到特朗普拥有更大权力（如核武器控制权）。

• **BirAdam**: 质疑如果取消SpaceX的合同，是否会对美国目前参与的代理战争和卫星网络造成影响，并指出波音或Blue Origin目前的发射成本更高。

• **kaycebasques**: 提到马斯克在共和党中很受欢迎，并提供了一个相关链接以支持这一观点。

• **bgwalter**: 认为特朗普与马斯克的冲突可能是戏剧化的表现，旨在吸引其MAGA基础选民的注意，实际上SpaceX仍将继续获得资助。

• **mystified5016**: 将冲突视为独裁者与其强大亲信之间的内斗，并认为这种现象过早出现可能表明领导 incompetence。

• **state_less**: 主张SpaceX合同应基于其对国家的服务质量和价格，而非个人冲突，并批评特朗普的某些法案对贫困人群的影响。

• **jmyeet**: 认为有关冲突的阴谋论反映了人们的心理认知失调，指出马斯克和特朗普均为自负且情绪化的人，冲突可能不仅仅是表面上的那么简单，并详细列举了特朗普可能采取的针对马斯克的极端措施。

• **ndr42**: 引用了有关性别偏见的研究，暗示对高政治职务上的男性不应持有特定偏见。

• **tonymet**: 表达了对马斯克与特朗普冲突导致立场混乱的困惑，尤其是对贴标签和破坏特斯拉行为的态度。

• **linotype**: 简单表示当前结果是可预测的，未展开详细论述。

• **tsoukase**: 以旁观者角度描述美国当前局势的戏剧性，担忧国家权力落入不可靠的人手中。

• **shrubble**: 提出马斯克与特朗普冲突可能是为转移公众注意力，以推动其他政策或法案通过。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于特朗普是否会基于个人恩怨而非实际表现来取消政府合同，以及这种做法是否会导致腐败和国家利益受损。
- 有人认为冲突可能是政治戏剧，旨在吸引选民注意，而其他人则担心这种冲突可能带来实际的负面影响。
- 阴谋论和心理分析也成为讨论的一部分，反映出公众对事件的复杂认知和情感反应。
- 还有人关注冲突对SpaceX等公司及相关政策的影响，以及对贫困人群的潜在影响。

44209515.article_content:
Elon Musk gestures while discussing the sixth Starship test launch with President-elect Donald Trump at Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas. To the right of Trump is Gen. Chance Saltzman, Chief of space operations for the U.S. Space Force. Credit: Brandon Bell/Getty Images
WASHINGTON — An escalating feud between President Trump and Elon Musk June 5 included threats to cancel SpaceX contracts and decommission spacecraft, although those words have yet to become actions.
In a heated exchange largely carried out on social media, Musk’s criticism of a budget reconciliation bill backed by Trump turned into full-fledged attacks on each other, less than a week after Musk ended his formal role in the administration as a “special government employee” overseeing the White House’s Department of Government Efficiency.
That exchange included a threat by Trump to cancel government contracts with Musk’s companies, such as SpaceX. “The easiest way to save money in our Budget, Billions and Billions of Dollars, is to terminate Elon’s Governmental Subsidies and Contracts,” Trump
posted
on his social media platform, Truth Social.
While the comment did not specifically mention SpaceX, Musk appeared to interpret it as a threat to SpaceX. “In light of the President’s statement about cancellation of my government contracts, @SpaceX will begin decommissioning its Dragon spacecraft immediately,” he
posted
on his social media platform, X, about 90 minutes later. He didn’t elaborate on what would be involved in “decommissioning” Dragon.
The back-and-forth between Musk and Trump raised fears that the White House might cut SpaceX off from its extensive work with NASA and the Defense Department, to the detriment of both the government and the company. It comes just months after many in the space industry worried that the then-close relationship between Musk and Trump might give SpaceX an unfair advantage.
Any loss of federal contracts would have a significant effect on SpaceX. Musk, in a rare glimpse into SpaceX finances,
said
June 3 that SpaceX is projecting $15.5 billion in revenue in 2025, of which $1.1 billion would come from NASA contracts. He did not disclose the amount coming from defense work, which would include launches as well as Starlink services and development of a reconnaissance satellite constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office.
The effects on the government from canceling those contracts, though, could be far greater. Both NASA and the Defense Department rely heavily on SpaceX for launch services as competing vehicles from other companies have been slow to enter service. SpaceX has the only operational vehicle, other than Russia’s Soyuz, to get crews to and from the International Space Station, and is a key cargo supplier. SpaceX also has a NASA contract to develop the U.S. Deorbit Vehicle, the spacecraft that will ensure a safe reentry of the station at the end of its life.
One industry source, speaking on background, dismissed the exchanges as “bluster” that neither Musk nor Trump would actually implement, noting the reliance the federal government has on SpaceX and SpaceX’s desire to retain government revenue.
Indeed, Musk, about five hours after making the threat to decommission Dragon, walked it back. “Good advice,” he wrote in a
post
, responding to a pseudonymous user who asked Musk to “cool off and take a step back for a couple days” from the debate. “Ok, we won’t decommission Dragon.”
NASA stood on the sidelines during the Trump-Musk exchanges. “NASA will continue to execute upon the President’s vision for the future of space. We will continue to work with our industry partners to ensure the President’s objectives in space are met,” said NASA press secretary Bethany Stevens.
Search for new NASA administrator nominee
The dispute between Musk and Trump overshadowed comments made by Trump earlier in the day about
his decision announced May 31 to withdraw the nomination of Jared Isaacman to be NASA administrator
.
Musk “wanted, and rightfully, recommended somebody that I guess he knew very well — I’m sure he respected him — to run NASA, and I didn’t think it was appropriate,” Trump said in a media availability with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Trump said that Isaacman was a Democrat, although Isaacman has donated to both Republican and Democratic candidates and organizations over the year.
“We won. We get certain privileges and one of the privileges is we don’t have to appoint a Democrat,” Trump said.
“NASA is very important. We have great people. Gen. Caine is going to be picking somebody. We’ll be checking him out,” he said, a reference to Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. It’s unclear why Trump asked Caine, an Air Force general with no space background, to select the head of the nation’s civil space agency.
Related
Jeff Foust
Jeff Foust writes about space policy, commercial space, and related topics for SpaceNews.
He earned a Ph.D. in planetary sciences from the Massachusetts Instit

data.title: Washington Post's Privacy Tip: Stop Using Chrome, Delete Meta Apps (and Yandex)
data.author: miles
data.article_summary: 《华盛顿邮报》科技专栏作家报道，Meta的Facebook和Instagram应用程序通过数字后门获取用户数据长达数月，规避了谷歌为Android设备设置的隐私保护。研究显示，Mozilla Firefox、Brave浏览器和DuckDuckGo能有效阻止许多追踪方法，而Chrome不能。Safari也提供较强的隐私保护。建议删除手机上的Meta和Yandex应用程序，因为它们能收集更多信息，如位置、电池状态等。即使不使用Meta的应用，Meta仍可能收集用户的网络活动信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对隐私保护、浏览器选择及网络追踪问题的讨论

不同观点：
• [xnx] 认为不推荐使用广告拦截器（adblocker）的建议不可信，暗示广告拦截器是保护隐私的必要工具。
• [aucisson_masque] 认为谷歌并未真正关心安卓用户的隐私，即使问题对用户和公司都有利，谷歌也没有采取行动。他提出使用iPhone、GrapheneOS或不用手机作为解决方案。
• [ThinkBeat] 对华盛顿邮报文章中的“Meta追踪代码”感到困惑，认为该代码只是追踪访问的网站，而不是捕捉所有网页内容。
• [meroes] 讨论了因工作需要被迫使用Chrome浏览器的情况，并询问是否可以通过购买工作手机来获得税收优惠。
• [m-localhost] 分享了自己使用不同浏览器的经验，如Firefox和Edge，但仍未找到替代Chrome在网页开发方面的合适选择。
• [helph67] 引用了TechRadar的文章，指出问题在三十个月后仍未改善，暗示隐私问题长期存在。
• [p0w3n3d] 提到Chrome的最新版本不允许直接下载PDF文件，只能保存到云端，这可能影响用户体验。
• [thadk] 询问如何避免在手机上使用WhatsApp应用，可能出于隐私保护的考虑。
• [dlachausse] 提到Safari浏览器阻止了华盛顿邮报主页上的16个追踪器，认为从隐私角度看，最好避免访问此类网站。
• [bn-l] 寻找不崩溃且速度不慢的Chrome替代浏览器。
• [leereeves] 希望发起类似当年抵制Internet Explorer的“停止使用Chrome”运动，以推动隐私保护。
• [ChrisArchitect] 提供了相关讨论的链接，供其他用户参考。
• [keernan] 认为在一个真正民主的社会中，应该有严厉的法律惩罚任何形式的在线追踪行为，反映了对隐私保护立法的期望。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于谷歌和Meta等公司是否真正关心用户隐私。一些用户（如[aucisson_masque]）认为这些公司不重视隐私保护，而其他用户（如[ThinkBeat]）则对具体技术细节和追踪机制感到困惑。
• 用户对浏览器的选择和替代方案有不同看法，特别是对于Chrome的隐私问题和功能限制（如[p0w3n3d]、[bn-l]），同时也有用户分享了使用其他浏览器的经验（如[m-localhost]）。
• 一些用户（如[meroes]、[thadk]）讨论了具体场景下的隐私保护策略，如工作需要使用特定浏览器或避免使用特定应用。

44210689.article_content:
177950065
story
Meta's Facebook and Instagram apps "were
siphoning people's data through a digital back door
for months,"
writes a Washington Post tech columnist
, citing researchers who found no privacy setting could've stopped what Meta and Yandex were doing, since those two companies "circumvented privacy and security protections that Google set up for Android devices.
"But their tactics underscored some privacy vulnerabilities in web browsers or apps. These steps can reduce your risks."
Stop using the Chrome browser.
Mozilla's
Firefox
, the
Brave
browser and
DuckDuckGo
's browser block many common methods of tracking you from site to site. Chrome, the most popular web browser, does not... For iPhone and Mac folks, Safari also has strong privacy protections.
It's not perfect
, though.  No browser protections are foolproof. The researchers said Firefox on Android devices was partly susceptible to the data harvesting tactics they identified, in addition to Chrome. (DuckDuckGo and Brave largely did block the tactics, the researchers said....)
Delete Meta and Yandex apps on your phone, if you have them.
The tactics described by the European researchers showed that Meta and Yandex are unworthy of your trust. (Yandex is not popular in the United States.)    It might be wise to delete their apps, which give the companies more latitude to collect information that websites generally cannot easily obtain, including your approximate location, your phone's battery level and what other devices, like an Xbox, are connected to your home WiFi.
Know, too, that even if you don't have Meta apps on your phone, and even if you don't use Facebook or Instagram at all, Meta might still harvest information on your activity across the web.

data.title: My experiment living in a tent in Hong Kong's jungle
data.author: 5mv2
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某人在大学期间通过帐篷生活节省开支的实验的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• Hnrobert42：赞赏该实验的细节，认为学校环境使得实验与单纯的帐篷生活不同。学费类似于租金，提供了淋浴、电力和有空调的公共空间，以及支持性社区。学校和社会更倾向于帮助贫困学生，而非试图减少房租的成年人。
• paxys：认为投资回报（ROI）的计算过于短视。学费已经支付，获得教育有助于偿还贷款。为了基本生活需求而增加的支出是值得的，长期的“流浪汉式”生活不切实际，会对学业产生负面影响。

• danielvf：指出在潮湿夏季，电力和小风扇对露营体验的改善。
• daedrdev：提到UC Berkeley有 homeless学生。
• ambicapter：认为“社区支持”部分很感人。
• throe83949449：批评高调的帐篷搭建方式，认为应低调以避免影响他人。

• verall：赞赏实验地点的美景。
• lazyeye：质疑在旧金山通过住在货车中节省开支的可行性。

data.title: Why Pandas feels clunky when coming from R (2024)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 这篇文章比较了使用R语言的tidyverse和Python的pandas进行数据分析的体验。作者作为一个R语言的坚定支持者，在必须使用Python工作五年后，仍然觉得pandas操作不如tidyverse流畅。文章通过一个简单的购买数据分析示例，逐步展示了如何在R和Python中完成相同的任务。在R中，使用tidyverse的管道操作符可以很直观地进行数据处理、分组和汇总，而在Python中，尽管pandas也能完成相同任务，但代码较为冗长，且有多种实现方式，不如R直观。作者认为，对于习惯tidyverse的人来说，解释pandas的不足之处往往是困难的，因为pandas在Python数据科学中已被广泛接受为强大工具，但其使用体验仍不如tidyverse流畅。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同编程语言和工具在数据科学和科学计算中的优缺点，特别是Python和R，以及相关的替代工具。

不同观点：
• dleather认为Python在数据科学和科学计算中的工作流比较繁琐，尤其是包的选择和不同包之间的语法差异让人困惑。他建议需要一个统一的框架，并认为如果不是因为Python在行业中的广泛应用，Julia可能会是更好的选择。
• emehex怀念R中的dplyr和hadleyverse，并尝试创建一个名为"redframes"的包来解决Pandas中的问题，但未获得广泛使用。
• ryan-duve建议如果了解Pandas的`.eval`方法，可能会减少Pandas使用中的笨重感，并提供了一个具体的代码示例。
• BDPW从R转到Python，认为R在处理复杂或不常见数据操作时让人沮丧，因为难以了解底层数据操作的细节。
• great_wubwub使用Polars代替Pandas，感觉更顺畅，并询问Polars与R的比较。
• btown推荐使用Malloy，这是一种领域特定语言，强调管道化操作，并与SQL和BI工具兼容。
• dkdcio提到Ibis，这是一个由Pandas创始人创建的工具，解决了Pandas的许多问题。
• __mharrison__提到其书《Effective Pandas》帮助读者更好地适应Pandas，并表达了对Pandas的强烈看法。
• wodenokoto指出RStudio的强大功能，如自动完成变量名，是R的一大优势。
• smabie认为Pandas的行索引是其主要缺陷。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个工具和包，如redframes、Polars、Malloy、Ibis，以及它们在数据处理中的应用和优缺点。
• 争议的焦点主要在于Pandas的复杂性和笨重感，以及是否需要一个统一的框架来简化数据科学工作流。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是R和Python在不同场景下的优劣，以及用户对各自生态系统的偏好。

44210614.article_content:
Five years ago I started a new role and I suddenly found myself, a
staunch R fan, having to code in Python on a daily basis. Working with
data, most of my Python work involved using
pandas
, the Python data frame library,
and initially I found it quite hard and clunky to use, being used to the
silky smooth
API of R’s
tidyverse
. And
you know what? It still feels hard and clunky, even now, 5 years later!
But, what seems even harder, is explaining to “Python people” what they
are missing out on. From their perspective, pandas is this fantastic
tool that makes Data Science in Python possible. And it is a fantastic
tool, don’t get me wrong, but if you, like me, end up in many “pandas is
great, but…”-type discussions and are lacking clear examples to link to;
here’s a somewhat typical example of a simple analysis, built from the
ground up, that flows nicely in R and the tidyverse but that becomes
clunky and complicated using Python and pandas.
Let’s first step through a short analysis of purchases using R and the
tidyverse. After that we’ll see how the same solution using Python and
pandas compares.
Analyzing
purchases
in R
We’ve been given a table of
purchases
with different
amount
s, where the customer could have received a
discount
and where
each purchase happened in a
country
. Finance now wants to know: How
much do we typically sell in each country? Let’s read in the data and
take a look:
library
(tidyverse)
purchases
<-
read_csv
(
"purchases.csv"
)
purchases
|>
head
()
# A tibble: 6 × 3
country amount discount
<chr>    <dbl>    <dbl>
1 USA       2000       10
2 USA       3500       15
3 USA       3000       20
4 Canada     120       12
5 Canada     180       18
6 Canada    3100       21
Now, without bothering with printing out the intermediate results,
here’s how a quick pipeline could be built up, answering Finance’s
question.
“How much do we sell..? Let’s take the total sum!”
purchases
$
amount
|>
sum
()
“Ah, they wanted it by country…”
purchases
|>
group_by
(country)
|>
summarize
(total
=
sum
(amount))
“And I guess I should deduct the discount.” (
#👈/👆/👇
marks lines
that changed/moved)
purchases
|>
group_by
(country)
|>
summarize
(total
=
sum
(amount
-
discount))
#👈
“Oh, and Maria asked me to remove any outliers. Let’s remove everything
10x larger than the median.”
purchases
|>
filter
(amount
<=
median
(amount)
*
10
)
|>
#👈
group_by
(country)
|>
summarize
(total
=
sum
(amount
-
discount))
“I probably should use the median
within
each country. Prices are
quite different across the globe…”
purchases
|>
group_by
(country)
|>
#👆
filter
(amount
<=
median
(amount)
*
10
)
|>
#👇
summarize
(total
=
sum
(amount
-
discount))
# A tibble: 11 × 2
country   total
<chr>     <dbl>
1 Australia   540
2 Brazil      414
3 Canada      270
4 France      450
5 Germany     513
6 India       648
7 Italy       567
8 Japan       621
9 Spain       594
10 UK          432
11 USA        8455
“And we’re done, let’s go for second breakfast!”
Analyzing
purchases
in Python
We’re now going to take a look at how this little analysis would look in
Python and pandas. One complication here is that pandas can be written
in many different styles; it’s not like in the tidyverse where there’s
often one obvious way to do something. Here we’re opting for writing
pandas using the fluent method chaining API, as opposed to using the
more “imperative” approach that results in a lot of repeats of
df
and
statements like
df[df["this"] == "that"] = calc_some(df["other_thing"])
. We’re also
opting for always returning a table with all the data in the data frame
proper. We don’t want data hidden away in the index (that is, pandas’
really advanced system for row and column names). Having data in the
index is generally annoying when one wants to process the data further
or when turning the data into plots.
Again, let’s step through the R version of the analysis, and below let’s
write the corresponding pandas code. Again,
#👈/👆/👇
marks lines that
have changed/moved.
Reading in the data
# R
library
(tidyverse)
purchases
<-
read_csv
(
"purchases.csv"
)
purchases
|>
head
()
# A tibble: 6 × 3
country amount discount
<chr>    <dbl>    <dbl>
1 USA       2000       10
2 USA       3500       15
3 USA       3000       20
4 Canada     120       12
5 Canada     180       18
6 Canada    3100       21
This is basically the same in pandas. So far so good!
# Python
import
pandas
as
pd
purchases
=
pd
.
read_csv(
"purchases.csv"
)
purchases
.
head()
country  amount  discount
0     USA    2000        10
1     USA    3500        15
2     USA    3000        20
3  Canada     120        12
4  Canada     180        18
“How much do we sell..? Let’s take the total sum!”
# R
purchases
$
amount
|>
sum
()
[1] 17210
This is also similar in pandas:
# Python
purchases[
"amount"
]
.
sum()
17210
(However, note that this method,
pandas.Series.sum()
,
is not the same as
pandas.DataFrame.sum()
,
or
numpy.sum()
,
or the built-in
sum
function, each of which has different arguments and behaviors. In R

data.title: Updates to Advanced Voice Mode for paid users
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ChatGPT语音模式的更新及其引发的问题和用户反馈

不同观点：
• zaptrem和tallytarik提到语音模式中偶尔会出现幻觉现象，产生类似广告、胡言乱语或背景音乐的声音。zaptrem认为这可能是由于模型在播客数据上训练以获得自然语调所致，并对此现象感到好奇。
• kubb最初认为高级语音模式比之前更差，声音显得冷漠且语调怪异，但在进一步使用后认为新语音尚可接受，只是仍具有明显的人工痕迹，并且有时会错误解读用户的输入。
• nickthegreek和kubb有类似感受，认为更新后的语音模式变得更差，表现出冷漠和犹豫不决的特点，并对此感到失望。nickthegreek最终换用了Maple语音。
• TheTaytay怀念仅包含文本转语音和语音转文本的旧版语音模式，认为高级语音模式经常出错，而底层模型的智能表现更好。
• dedicate表示在日常使用中，只想要一个能给出答案的智能助手，而不是一个表演者，更希望语音模式听起来像一个聪明的助手，而不是最好的朋友。
• nikkwong批评语音模式中的女性声音像“山谷女孩”，男性声音则类似，并希望能有更多样化和真实的声音选择，而不是明显由旧金山单一文化开发的产品。
• ed_mercer更喜欢标准语音模式Cove的稳重声音，认为高级Cove的声音过于快乐，希望能有更多语音风格的控制选项。
• patwolf注意到新语音更显懒散并添加了更多的“嗯”，但认为这只是需要适应的问题，同时提到语音模式仍能执行一些有趣的功能，如模仿Ent说话。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Atkinson算法及其应用（特别是B&W抖动效果）以及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun分享了个人经历，认为Atkinson算法在B&W抖动效果中表现出色，并提到了该算法在个人项目中的实际应用，比如为Mac shareware游戏创建logo以及在eInk项目中使用该算法处理月亮图片。
• AndrewStephens赞同JKCalhoun的观点，认为Atkinson抖动在老式Mac显示器上的表现特别好，并提到自己也在项目中使用该算法，还发现今日网页组件访问量增加可能与某个悲伤的新闻有关。
• throwanem从技术角度提出改进建议，指出可以通过为下载文件设置默认名称和.png扩展名来优化用户体验，并提供了相关的开发者文档链接。
• minorbug分享了自己正在开发的项目，该项目可以将多张图片转换为MacPaint格式，并提供了GitHub链接和使用Gemini Deep Research库的细节。

补充讨论：
• nedt提醒用户不要点击某个链接，因为该链接指向的页面可能包含不适宜内容，暗示链接内容未及时更新。
• amelius提供了使用Python实现类似功能的GitHub项目链接。
• deverman简单表达了对使用自己喜欢照片进行实验的兴趣。
• franze分享了自己创建的关于Atkinson算法的学习资源，并表示经过AI校对以确保事实准确。
• larodi提出了一个疑问，是否讨论的Atkinson与近日去世的人是同一人，暗示讨论可能是一个纪念。
• kgbcia认为该算法非常适合用于eInk/epaper设备。
• RodgerTheGreat分享了自己多年前编写的类似工具，并提供了链接。
• ksr赞赏了UI设计，并提供了演示的GitHub链接。
• gcanyon提出了自己在使用过程中遇到的问题，即无法正确导出文件。
• zdw指出工具中的一个尺寸选项与原版Mac分辨率不一致，提出了对历史准确性的关注。

• 链接内容的适宜性（nedt提出的NSFW问题）。
• 工具使用中遇到的实际问题（gcanyon的文件导出问题）。
• 对Atkinson算法相关信息的准确性（franze的AI校对声明）。

data.title: Self-Host and Tech Independence: The Joy of Building Your Own
data.author: articsputnik
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在技术自托管和科技独立方面的个人经历与感悟。作者受到PewDiePie安装Arch Linux和自制设备的启发，探讨了自己构建和托管服务的重要性。作者强调，拥有自己的域名和博客网站能够积累长期价值，避免频繁更换平台导致的内容流失。他分享了自己自托管博客、第二大脑、书籍、订阅列表等的经验，并介绍了如何通过学习Linux等基础知识实现技术独立。作者认为，自建和使用开源软件不仅能带来成就感，还能避免陷入订阅制消费的困境。文章最后鼓励读者从购买自己的域名开始，逐步探索技术独立的可能性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自托管（self-hosting）的价值、方法、挑战和相关工具

不同观点：
• **支持自托管，强调硬件再利用和低成本**：[kassner] 认为旧硬件（如旧笔记本电脑）可以有效用于Linux服务器，无需购买新设备，尤其在能效方面优于台式机。他分享了自己使用2011年i3处理器的笔记本电脑进行自托管的经历，并指出这是一种经济且可持续的选择。

• **推荐使用Proxmox进行虚拟化和容器化管理**：[briHass] 建议使用Proxmox作为自托管的基础工具，通过LXC容器和虚拟机管理服务。他认为LXC比Docker更容易管理，并且Proxmox提供的自动化备份和磁盘共享功能非常实用。

• **自托管的麻烦和维护成本**：[aucisson_masque] 指出自托管虽然可以节省费用，但需要面对频繁的更新和故障排除，有时会浪费大量时间。他表示，如果服务商价格合理且尊重隐私，宁愿付费使用服务。

• **自托管与离线生产力**：[sunshine-o] 分享了自己在互联网中断期间通过自托管提升生产力的体验，指出离线自托管可以减少对外部网络的依赖，但也提到如NixOS在离线环境下的局限性。

• **SBC（单板计算机）在自托管中的应用**：[kldg] 提到使用Raspberry Pi作为网络服务器的经验，强调其节能优势，但也指出需要时刻关注资源使用情况。他还提到高规格设备在网络服务器应用中的尴尬境地。

• **域名和网络身份的脆弱性**：[sdf4j] 提醒大家即使自托管，域名和互联网接入仍是租用的，强调在线身份的脆弱性。

• **自托管工具的现代便利性**：[arjie] 认为现代自托管工具使得自托管变得更容易，可以从托管服务逐步切换到自托管，分享了自己使用Cloudflare和本地NAS的混合方案。

• **自托管的潜在监管风险**：[budududuroiu] 担心开源和自托管的普及可能会引发大公司的反扑和监管限制，类似于比尔·盖茨曾经对爱好者的批评。

• **自托管的能力而非强制性**：[klabb3] 提出自托管应是一种能力而非必须，这样更具包容性，可以让技术能力较弱或愿意付费的人有更多选择，同时强调迁移服务的能力以避免被锁定。

补充讨论：
• **GNU项目在自由软件中的贡献**：[davidcalloway] 指出文章中未提及GNU项目，认为自由软件不应仅归功于Linus Torvalds。

• **开放源代码的邮件服务器**：[igtztorrero] 推荐PostalServer作为开源的大量事务性邮件发送工具。

• **现代LLM（大型语言模型）对自托管的促进作用**：[NicoSchwandner] 和 [larodi] 提到现代LLM使得自托管变得更加容易和有趣，可能会成为一种趋势。

• **自托管作为在线身份的保护手段**：[ryandrake] 强调自托管可以减少依赖大型平台而无法追索的风险，例如Gmail账户丢失，指出自托管自己的电子邮件身份至关重要。

• **Arch Linux安装的简化**：[Havoc] 提到Arch Linux现在有了安装程序，安装过程不再像以前那么困难，但仍需要面对命令行界面。

争议焦点：
• **自托管的利弊**：一些人如[aucisson_masque]强调自托管的麻烦和维护成本，而另一些人如[kassner]和[briHass]则强调其经济性和可控性。
• **自托管的普及与监管**：[budududuroiu]担心自托管的普及可能会引发大公司的反扑和监管限制。

Contents
Self-Host & Tech Independence: The Joy of Building Your Own
A personal journey.
Productivity
2025-06-07
2168 words
11 minutes
Contents
After watching the two
PewDiePie
videos where he learned about
installing Arch
(something considered quite hard, even for Linux enthusiasts) and
building three products
(camera for the dog, weather/drinking/meditation device, and who knows what comes next) based on open-source, 3D-printed parts, I started wondering about building things yourself, self-hosting, and tech independence. Something dear to my heart for a while.
If people ask me how they should start writing or how to get a job, I always say to buy a domain first. Secondly, host your own blog website if you have the technical skills (although it’s not so hard anymore). Because all of this compounds over time. Of course, you can start with a ready-made blog and a URL not yours, but if you want to do it long term, I saw many people changing from
WordPress
to Medium to Substack to Ghost, so what’s next? Over that time, sometimes they didn’t migrate their long-effort blog posts but started new.
Every time they had a new domain. To me, that’s so sad. Of course, you have learned a lot, and sometimes it’s also good to start new, but imagine instead if that happened over 10 years. If you compare that 10-year blog that has the same domain, keeping hard-earned backlinks, showcasing your long-term investment with old blog posts, even though they might not be as good as current ones (but doesn’t that happen all the time), what a huge difference that would be?
As someone who has hosted my own stuff for quite a while, and has been adding more every year, I thought I would write a short article about it.
My Own Story
I self-host
my blog
,
my second brain
,
my book
,
my subscriber list
(with
Listmonk
), implemented my own paywall with
Memberstack
, and have had my own website and blog for almost all my life (started my own domain, built WordPress,
moved
to
GoHugo
).
Lately, I also went into Homelab and built my own Home Server with SSH, backup, photos, Gitea, etc. Setting up my own configuration for Reverse Proxy and SSL Certificates for my Homeserver, creating SSL certificates, setting up SSH keys to SSH into without a loginâall great things you learn along the way.
Initially everything seems hard, but once you know how, it’s kind of obvious and less hard. It’s also, as ThePrimeagen
says
, that there is always a big part of
ignorance
where one tells themselves, “Oh that can’t be that hard”. But then you realize it’s much harder than you thought. But once you overcome the first hurdles, it’s really rewarding, and once working, it just works!
Most of what inspires me to do more is the joy of using something you built yourself, and usually not paying for it. Maybe this is also because of the subscription hell we are living in, where every single app or service can’t be used without a subscription.
How it Started for Me
When I got into
vim
, and especially
Neovim
, all of a sudden I lived in the terminal and knew some of the commands that usually only Linux wizards or nerds know, but now I am one myself :) But with great pride. Find more on my journey on my
PKM Workflow Blog
.
Tech Independence
Tech Independence is something I
learned
from Derek Sivers, and basically means that you do
not depend on any particular company or software
.
The premise is that by learning some of the fundamentals, in this case
Linux
, you can host most things yourself. Not because you need to, but because you want to, and the feeling of using your own services just gives you pleasure. And you learn from it. Derek goes deep in his article. He self-hosts email, contacts & calendar, and your own backup storage. But you can start small. We always believe we just have to use what’s out there to buy, but there are other ways.
Start by buying your own domain today. Put some thought into the name, but don’t overcomplicate it. If you have any success or links whatsoever, you can always move the domain later if you don’t like it (and forward existing blogs to a new domain with not much lost). But you can’t do it if you don’t have your own domain or own hosted server.
Open-Source
Most of it is
Open-Source
and comes when you dabble in Linux. As the story of PewDiePie shows, once you learn Linux, you want to build everything yourself and not pay for anything ð.
Open-source and open-source code is beautiful. It’s much more than just using someone else’s software, but it’s all the millions of people who just give away their work for free. It’s a community of people working for everyone. By putting it on GitHub, people can give feedback (issues) or contribute (Pull Requests), and you as the owner can or cannot listen to it. It’s your choice. Like in the real world.
But most of all, everyone can use your code for free. Some nuances on the licensing, but if you have MIT or some other permissive
License
, everyone can use it.

Actually, my

• **SBC（单板计算机）在自托管中的应用**：[kldg] 提到使用Raspberry Pi作为网络服务器的经验，强调其节能优势，但也指出需要时刻关注资源使用情况。他还提到高规格设备在网络服务器应用中的尴尬境地。

• **域名和网络身份的脆弱性**：[sdf4j] 提醒大家即使自托管，域名和互联网接入仍是租用的，强调在线身份的脆弱性。

• **自托管工具的现代便利性**：[arjie] 认为现代自托管工具使得自托管变得更容易，可以从托管服务逐步切换到自托管，分享了自己使用Cloudflare和本地NAS的混合方案。

• **自托管的潜在监管风险**：[budududuroiu] 担心开源和自托管的普及可能会引发大公司的反扑和监管限制，类似于比尔·盖茨曾经对爱好者的批评。

• **自托管的能力而非强制性**：[klabb3] 提出自托管应是一种能力而非必须，这样更具包容性，可以让技术能力较弱或愿意付费的人有更多选择，同时强调迁移服务的能力以避免被锁定。

补充讨论：
• **GNU项目在自由软件中的贡献**：[davidcalloway] 指出文章中未提及GNU项目，认为自由软件不应仅归功于Linus Torvalds。

• **开放源代码的邮件服务器**：[igtztorrero] 推荐PostalServer作为开源的大量事务性邮件发送工具。

• **现代LLM（大型语言模型）对自托管的促进作用**：[NicoSchwandner] 和 [larodi] 提到现代LLM使得自托管变得更加容易和有趣，可能会成为一种趋势。

• **自托管作为在线身份的保护手段**：[ryandrake] 强调自托管可以减少依赖大型平台而无法追索的风险，例如Gmail账户丢失，指出自托管自己的电子邮件身份至关重要。

• **Arch Linux安装的简化**：[Havoc] 提到Arch Linux现在有了安装程序，安装过程不再像以前那么困难，但仍需要面对命令行界面。

争议焦点：
• **自托管的利弊**：一些人如[aucisson_masque]强调自托管的麻烦和维护成本，而另一些人如[kassner]和[briHass]则强调其经济性和可控性。
• **自托管的普及与监管**：[budududuroiu]担心自托管的普及可能会引发大公司的反扑和监管限制。

data.title: BorgBackup 2 has no server-side append-only anymore
data.author: jaegerma
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了BorgBackup项目中移除对仅追加（append-only）存储支持的更改。仅追加功能依赖于服务器端组件来强制执行，因为这只能在服务器端控制，而不能在客户端控制。在Borg 1.x中，只有使用SSH的仓库支持该功能，而在Borg 2中，包括文件系统、SFTP、Rclone、S3/B3等仓库类型并不具备服务器端强制执行的能力。目前的解决方案建议通过存储层限制删除权限来实现仅追加功能，例如`borg create`使用无删除权限的凭证，而`borg compact`则使用有删除权限的凭证。有开发者对该方案的安全性提出疑问，认为需要某种形式的仅追加支持以防止数据被恶意篡改。

不同观点：
• antoniomika和ThomasWaldmann（BorgBackup开发者）指出，Borg 1.x中的“仅追加”模式由于存储机制的变化在Borg 2中被移除，但通过新的权限控制功能（如"no-delete"和"write-only"）提供了更灵活的保护选项。他们认为这些新功能可以替代并超越原先的“仅追加”模式。

• aborsy关注Borg 2的beta测试时间，显示出对软件稳定性和发布时间的关心。
• TheFreim和jbverschoor则在更广泛地讨论备份工具的选择，考虑其他替代方案如Duplicacy。
• nathants和puffybuf主张简化备份方案，避免过度复杂化，并提到使用文件系统层级的加密和自动清理脚本。
• LeoPanthera建议使用ZFS不可变快照或其他文件系统功能来实现类似保护，认为这是一种更基础的解决方案。

• 关于Borg 2中权限控制的实现，ThomasWaldmann提供了多个相关代码链接，并建议用户查阅文档以避免混淆。
• 讨论中多次提到勒索软件和客户端被攻破的情景，显示出用户对备份安全性的高度重视。
• 不同用户对备份工具的偏好和使用经验各异，从BorgBackup、Restic到自定义脚本和ZFS快照，反映了备份方案选择的多样性。

争议焦点：
• Borg 2移除“仅追加”模式是否会削弱其安全性，以及新引入的权限控制功能是否足够作为替代方案。
• 如何在备份系统中实现更细粒度的权限控制，以防止客户端被攻破后数据被覆盖或删除。

总结：讨论主要围绕BorgBackup及其替代工具的功能变化和安全性展开，特别是“仅追加”模式的替代方案和权限控制的实现。用户分享了各自的配置经验和工具偏好，反映了备份方案选择的多样性。争议点集中在Borg 2的安全性改进是否足够以及权限控制的细粒度管理上。

Some features like append-only repositories rely on a server-side component that enforces them (because that shall only be controllable server-side, not client-side).
So, that can only work, if such a server-side component exists, which is the case for borg 1.x ssh: repositories (but not for borg 1.x non-ssh: repositories).
For borg2, we currently have:
fs repos
sftp: repos
rclone: repos (enabling many different cloud providers)
s3/b3: repos
ssh: repos using client/server rpc code similar as in borg 1.x
So, only for the last method we have a borg server-side process that could enforce some features, but not for any of the other repo types.
For append-only the current idea is that this should not be done within borg, but solved by a missing repo object delete permission enforced by the storage.
borg create could then use credentials that miss permission to delete, while borg compact would use credentials that include permission to delete.
